intro.text: A hunter from a family of hunters, four years on the road to reach this door. His name is in the Count's ledger, and it is not struck through.

blocks.text: • Vampire hunter by family trade; Investigation and Survival; a suit built for this work.
• Reads hunters' chalk marks (Esmeralda's) and knows a baited snare on sight.
• Class: (check) ranger, fighter or a hunter build; the scripts give him advantage against baited traps and the training to read a vampire's patience.
• Player: (fill in)
• The study ledger of hunter families: most struck through. His family is there, not struck, with a date beside it. The date is this year.
• Strahd: "Four years on the road, is it not? I have guests who have stayed four hundred."
• Esmeralda's chalk mark on the study door frame: safe for now, do not linger.
• The dead adventurer in the false treasury wears a wolf's-tooth hunter token. So does Esmeralda. So does his family.
• A statue in the hall of heroes has his jaw and brow. A hunter of his blood came here and stayed.
• Lief's fair copy of the ledger: an ancestor marked received, with a crypt number.
• A crypt with his family name: bones laid out with respect, a silvered weapon, a letter that begins, "If you are reading this, he let me write it."
• To finish what his family started, and to learn what happened to the one who got this far.
• To decide what a hunter does with Emil, a werewolf unarmed behind bars and asking for help.
• Strahd knew a hunter was coming. The ledger was open before dinner.
• The Count respects very few people. The buried ancestor was one.
• Strahd's goal for him: learn the family's secrets.
• He hears the elevator trap a breath early: one word before it goes.
• Give him advantage to spot the treasury snare, and a check to see the catacomb floor is too clean.
• Spotlight: the ledger, the chalk mark, the statue, the crypt, the coffin ("stake, sunlight, running water").

intro.text: Halfling bard. Hears the shape of a piece of music and wants, very badly, to ring the bell.

blocks.text: • Halfling (bell rope "at halfling height"; swimming in three feet of water).
• Bard: Performance and History; passes as a witches' customer; reads verse aloud and gets the rhyme.
• Spelling: the scripts say Batrdlebee; the player may spell it Bardlebee. (check)
• Player: (fill in)
• The organ: Performance or History DC 13 tells him it is a long requiem, an hour left, and not for the Count himself.
• Strahd: "You heard where I stopped. Tell me how it should end." A good answer buys the party a favour.
• Escher trades truth for stories, and Batrdlebee gets two answers per story.
• The brazier verse: he reads it aloud and gets the rhyme, advantage on choosing right.
• The bell in the belfry, tied in a neat bow, within his reach. If it rings, every box ticks.
• To finish the Count's unfinished music, or to be the one who gets to say how it ends.
• An audience, including the one at the organ.
• The bell has not rung since the wedding day.
• Strahd's goal for him: win the bard.
• Spotlight: the bell, the unfinished music, Escher's gossip, the verse.
• Let him choose about the bell. Do not take it away from him.
• One barrel in the wine cellar sounds wrong when knocked: Perception DC 12 is his.

intro.text: Half vampire, wholly devout. His pulse falls into step with the organ and he hates that it does. The castle keeps asking him who made him.

blocks.text: • Dhampir; holy symbol; Turn Undead; Medicine and Arcana (from the scripts).
• Class: (check) cleric or paladin; the scripts use Turn Undead and a blessing of holy water.
• Player: (fill in)
• Strahd, quietly: "Who made you? I should like to know which of my kind was so careless."
• Escher: "Half! How economical. Do you get half the hunger, or all of it and half the teeth?"
• The bath: he smells it from the corridor. Ask his player what the hunger feels like, and whether the others notice him swallow.
• The witches have been asked to brew something for a guest with half a vampire's blood.
• The Heart of Sorrow beats with his pulse: every hit on it costs him a hit point, and he has advantage against it.
• The statues in the hall of heroes turn their eyes away from him, every one.
• An answer to who made him, and the strength not to need it.
• To be useful against the dead without becoming more like them.
• Sergei's tomb is the one place in the castle at peace. Evander feels it. A long rest there is safe.
• His symbol is cold on the catacombs' wrong consecrated ground. It still works.
• The Count's goal for him: find out who sired him.
• Turn Undead is his room in the guard barracks and buys two rounds in the drowned chamber. On Strahd in his own house it earns a smile.
• Spoiling the coffin's earth with holy water is his rite: three uninterrupted rounds.
• Spotlight: the bath, the Count's question, the heart, the tomb.

intro.text: Chief of a people, and the party's front line. He reads a hall the way a hunter reads a trail: who really runs it, who is watching, when the lord is busy.

blocks.text: • Leader of a people back home; speaks to lords and stewards as an equal (from the scripts).
• Fights with an axe; strong enough to tear a path through webs and break a broom over his knee.
• Class and ancestry: (check) the scripts imply a martial chief, likely fighter or barbarian.
• Player: (fill in)
• Strahd addresses him as one ruler to another: "You lead a people. So do I."
• The stone king in the hall of heroes speaks to him unasked: "I led ten thousand. Count who stands with me now."
• King Barov's tomb is the answer to that line: a king who built a kingdom and a son who buried it.
• The garrison officer salutes him as a visiting lord. Drilled men recognise him.
• Cyrus the cook responds to him as a steward to a chief: Persuasion at advantage when he speaks that way.
• To bring his people through, which tonight means bringing this party through.
• To be seen as a leader by the only other ruler in the valley, and to be ashamed of wanting that.
• The hall of bones is a hall furnished with the enemy dead. He understands the man who built it better than he wants to.
• The Count's goal for him: see if Torvald bends.
• Spotlight: the stone king, the garrison, the king's tomb, the broom.
• He will want to jump for the Heart of Sorrow. Tell him the odds, then let him.
• The bridge in the rain is his kind of fight: footing, no rail, a soldier on foot at the far end.
